text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- President's foreign policy powers should be divided into traditional and European Union issues: powers on domestic and EU issues should be limited, members of the Conservative party say at party conference.
- Budget cuts are necessary and the total sum of budget can move only downwards, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.
- Major companies should be taxed harder instead of budget cuts, says Green party deputy chairman Erkki Pulliainen. @
- Finland and Lithuania signed agreement to end visa requirements in September as Prime Minister Lipponen visited Lithuania.
KAUPPALEHTI
- After Nokia reported record first-half profits, a comparison of its profit and turnover figures show it is more profitable than its Swedish rival Ericsson.

- Merger between state-controlled oil group Neste and power group IVO would not create any significant synergy advantages, adviser Salomon Brothers says. No official comments have been given, but resistance towards a possible merger is believed to have increased inside IVO.
- Strengthening dollar and pound have profited Finnish exporting companies, especially forestries.
- State debt fell by three billion markka in May amounting to 431 billion markka in end of June, Finance Ministry says. @
AAMULEHTI
- Employment Ministry says computer and office labour sectors face recruiment problems: skilful ADP and office workers are hard to find despite high unemployment.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Strong demand for life insurance policies and the risks in capitalisation agreements have made insurer Suomi-Salama limit granting new life insurances.
DEMARI

- Index-link should be included in the pay agreement; but the destiny of the whole deal lays in the hands of the paper workers' union, says Per-Erik Lundh, chairman of the Finnish Metalworkers' Union.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Steven Thomas, an American with HIV jailed for attempted manslaughter after having unprotected sex without telling his partners he was infected, said in TV interview a good dose of racism was behind his 14-year jail sentence and he feels used.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
